text:
priya: Quick update: we launched prefetch-v3 + burst-throttle tuning to hosted canary (20% traffic) at 1724500000. Wanted to surface early numbers and the rollout plan. :rocket:

deploy-bot: release priya/prefetch-v3-burst-throttle -> canary (20%) succeeded. details: https://internal.redwood/deploys/1724500000

priya: Summary (canary vs baseline slice): p50 latency ~18% lower (45ms -> 37ms), p99 ~30% lower (240ms -> 168ms), average token cost per request ~14% lower. GPU utilization on the pool dropped ~9%.

ming: Nice. Do we have per-model or per-seq buckets? want to check LLM-heavy routes.

priya: Short answer: per-seq breakdown uploaded to runtime dashboard. Short and medium contexts (<=256 tokens) show biggest wins. Very long contexts (>=2048) show a small latency uptick (~4%) because batching windows changed; cost still improves there. Full breakdown: https://internal.redwood/telemetry/prefetch-v3-canary

jordan: Will this touch Dedicated/reserved fleets? Some enterprise teams pin large models next week.

priya: Not yet. We ran the change in a simulated dedicated environment and saw no quality regressions, but plan is: canary (20%) -> 50% hosted -> opt-in for Dedicated. We'll open an early-join form for dedicated owners who want to test.

kevin: Product: any customer-visible quality changes? e.g., generation jitter, tokenization differences?

priya: No behavioral changes to model outputs. This is purely serving-layer prefetch + adaptive burst control. Ran our eval-suite regressions and all clear. If you find a semantic change, tag #eng-runtime immediately.

sara: Rollout runbook posted: if canary p99 stays within SLA for 24h we move to 50% in 24h and full flip in 72h. Rollback key is pref_v3.enable=false and the immediate operator command is below.

```
# rollback toggle
redwoodctl rollout set pref_v3.enable=false --scope=hosted --selector=canary
```

kate: For customers using large embedding batches, did you measure batch sizes / memory headroom?

priya: Embedding batches increased ~12% which improved throughput; memory is within safety margins and alerts updated. I'll attach capacity matrices to the eng-runtime wiki after this post.

ming: Suggest adding a quick long-context smoke test to the canary pipeline so we catch regressions early.

priya: Good idea 1 — I'll add a 2-minute long-context smoke step to the canary job tonight. Targeting it live before we flip to 50%.

deploy-bot: canary health: 1724500000 -> healthy (35m), error rate below threshold, CPU/GPU steady.

priya: If you own latency-sensitive routes please check your per-route dashboards and comment on the runbook with any opt-out requests for Dedicated rollout. We'll share a short econ & latency retro after 72h with final numbers and follow-ups.

kevin: We'll watch customer telemetry and surface any opt-outs. Thanks for the heads-up.

jordan: Big win for runtime team. Congrats.

priya: Shoutout to the runtime folks who did the heavy lifting (Ming, Arif, Lena, Omar) 1. Excellent cross-team effort. :tada:

sara: I'll announce a 1-slide callout in tomorrow's all-hands with the headline numbers and link to the runbook.

kate: Please cc infra@ and product-sre@ when you flip to 50% so oncall can watch alerts.

priya: Will do. Thanks everyone."
